topics.title: Horizontal and vertical motions of ocean water

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the horizontal (currents, waves) and vertical (tides, upwelling, sinking) motions of ocean water.
Explain how wind gives energy to waves and why waves slow down and break near the shore.
Define wave crest, trough, height, amplitude, period, wavelength, speed and frequency.
Explain how the moon's and sun's gravity and the centrifugal force produce two tidal bulges.
Explain how continental shelves, islands, bays and estuaries modify tides and how tides differ from surges.
Distinguish semi-diurnal, diurnal and mixed tides.
Explain spring and neap tides from the relative positions of the sun, moon and earth.
Relate perigee, apogee, perihelion and aphelion to tidal range, and define ebb and flow.
Explain the uses of tides in navigation, fishing, desilting and tidal power.

topics.title: Ocean currents and the forces behind them

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how solar heating, wind, gravity and the Coriolis force start and steer ocean currents.
Explain how differences in temperature and salinity drive the sinking and rising of water.

topics.title: Types and major ocean currents
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Ocean Currents; Major Ocean Currents; Characteristics of Ocean Currents

concepts.learning_objective: Classify ocean currents by depth and by temperature and state where warm and cold currents usually flow.
Relate ocean circulation to atmospheric circulation and describe the drift (speed) of currents.
Explain how warm and cold currents affect the climate of coastal regions.
Explain why the mixing of warm and cold currents creates rich fishing grounds.
